media.description: Early twentieth-century postcard view of rue Alphonse-de-Neuville in the Plaine Monceau quarter of Paris. It provides period street context for the Polish Consulate General, located at number 19 in the late 1920s and 1930s; the postcard does not establish that the consulate building itself is visible.

timelineEvents.title: Arrival in New York en route to Los Angeles
timelineEvents.label: 24 Oct 1934 · Arrival in New York
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper arrives in New York from France with Eleonora, holding a temporary visa and travelling onward to Los Angeles.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Kaper and his wife Eleonora sailed from Le Havre on 17 October 1934 aboard the S.S. Champlain in second cabin class and reached New York on 24 October. Their non-immigrant visas had been issued in Paris on 15 October, numbered in a single series with the Jurmanns’ (NI 1581–1584), and the manifest records Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer as having paid the passage and as the party they were joining in Culver City. Kaper gave his occupation as musician and declared that he meant to stay about eight months and then return, without seeking United States citizenship. David Blum of the Culver Export Corporation met them in New York, and they left for Hollywood on 27 October.

timelineEvents.title: Legal Permanent Entry
timelineEvents.label: 1 Nov 1935 · Permanent U.S. entry
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper enters the United States for permanent residence through Calexico with Eleonora.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Enters for permanent residence at Calexico, California, from Mexicali on 1 November 1935, travelling on foot with Eleonora. The manifest records 6626 Franklin Ave., Hollywood, as his U.S. destination; his Declaration of Intention four months later records the same address as his residence. The crossing followed the Immigration and Naturalization Service pre-examination procedure: Kaper gave the Commercial Hotel in Mexicali as his last permanent residence abroad and entered on a consular immigration visa, C.I.V. no. 1/24, issued there under Section 5 of the Immigration Act of 1924 and charged to the Polish quota. The manifest records his previous stay in California from 24 October 1934 to 20 October 1935, and his Polish passport no. 10568, issued by the Consulate General in Paris on 5 August 1934 and expired on 25 August 1935.
